s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital and facial syndrome with mass effect
key_facts: History of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma
Treated with 4 cycles of ABVC and 3060 cGY radiation
Previous excisions of left upper eyelid mass
Multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells on histopathology
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme
MRI shows lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment
Tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery
Extension into the right cavernous sinus and right sphenoid sinus with mass effect on the left temporal lobe
Genetic testing shows splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the PALB2 gene

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, positive for CD68

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of the orbit and extension into the intracranial compartment, with histiocytic proliferation

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, with possible involvement of the orbit and intracranial compartment

shortlist.label: Histiocytic sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive clinical course with multiple recurrences and progression, with histiocytic proliferation

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells

shortlist.label: Giant cell reparative granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar histological features, including osteoclast-like giant cells and mononuclear cells

shortlist.label: Brown tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Possible relation to the osteoclast-like giant cells and mononuclear cells, although less likely given the clinical context

shortlist.label: Follicular dendritic cell sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible consideration given the histiocytic proliferation, although less likely than other options
